title: DR1 asks for the country of origin with a type-ahead search box under its own "Country of origin" subheading; the frontend uses a plain dropdown the user must scroll.

finding.frontend: Country of origin is a govuk-select rendered from src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/template.njk:15-22, labelled with a govuk-label--s label and opening on the placeholder "Select a country" followed by a disabled divider row. There is nothing to type into: the user opens the list and scrolls it.
finding.prototype: Country of origin sits under its own h2 subheading and is a search field — a text input placeheld "Search for a country" with a search button, which filters the country list as the user types and writes the chosen value into a hidden countryOfOrigin input. Only the destination-country question, which is a different control, uses a plain select in DR1.
finding.difference: Replace the origin country select with the same search-and-filter control, and promote its label to a subheading above the field. The prototype's version knows about parent countries — a territory is listed as "Azores (Portugal)" and carries Portugal as a parent — so the control should be built against a list of that shape rather than a flat one; that list is a separate finding and can land first or last. The frontend already ships a reusable type-ahead of this kind: src/server/common/components/accessible-autocomplete/macro.njk enhances a govukSelect into a type-ahead, and the port of entry field already uses it at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/port-of-entry/port-of-entry.njk:18-27. Applying that macro to countryOfOrigin is the smallest version of this change. It gives type-ahead filtering but not DR1's exact presentation — DR1 renders a search input with a magnifier button and its own results list, not an enhanced select — so decide which of the two the service is adopting before building it.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a text input or filter behaviour on the frontend's country-of-origin field — the captured DOM at fe-origin has a bare <select id="countryOfOrigin"> with 33 option elements and no input.
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs and opened both full-page screenshots side by side: fe-origin shows a narrow dropdown reading "Select a country", dr1-origin-of-the-import shows a full-width search box placeheld "Search for a country" with a blue magnifier button. Ran the falsifier — fe-origin has <select class="govuk-select" id="countryOfOrigin" name="countryOfOrigin"> with 33 options and no input of any kind in that form group. Re-resolved both citations at their lines: template.njk:15-22 is the govukSelect call with classes "govuk-label--s", origin-of-the-import.html:46-80 is the app-country-search wrapper. Confirmed the h2 subheading and the hidden countryOfOrigin input in DR1's markup. Rubric 4 checked against the country-list finding: distinct changes, the control against the list, not one increment. Rubric 9 fired on the last sentence of the difference slot. Slot fixed, claim otherwise CORRECT.
finding.correction: Claimed: "The frontend already ships a search-and-filter control of this kind for commodities, so the pattern exists in the codebase." The commodities half is false. fe-commodity-search renders nine checkbox inputs and one hidden crumb — no text input, no filter — and search.njk in the commodities feature contains no input other than the crumb. The feature directory is named `search` but the screen is a grouped checkbox list; the name is a route, not a control. Checked by listing every <input> in the captured DOM and grepping the template. The conclusion nevertheless survives and is stronger than the author had it: grepping for accessible-autocomplete across src/ found src/server/common/components/accessible-autocomplete/, a shared macro that enhances a govukSelect into a type-ahead, already consumed by the port-of-entry page. The difference slot has been rewritten to name that component and its existing use, and to flag that it is a type-ahead rather than DR1's bespoke search-and-results control. Also, under rubric 8, "countryOfOrigin" on the DR1 side is a hidden input; a visible-label control has been added so the crop has something to resolve to.

relatedTo.why: the search control filters the country list, and DR1's list has the parent-country shape the filter displays
